recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit as-is. Any further semantic refinement should be handled as a new BR&R decision rather than as unfinished FHIR-31850 application work.
issue_request: FHIR-31850 asked what ClinicalUseIssue/ClinicalUseDefinition indication.duration means and whether it describes treatment timing or the duration/offset of the indication criteria. The final Published/Persuasive with Modification decision required clarifying the definition and changing the element to ClinicalUseDefinition.indication.duration[x] using Range, with examples for myocardial infarction and ischaemic stroke.
initial_application: Commit 5cde06e72bec440f2436ad902c2709041280f22e applied FHIR#31850 by changing ClinicalUseDefinition.indication.duration to duration[x], replacing the old brief definition with the final example wording, and changing the type from Quantity to Range plus string. The current source still contains those changes.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini enables ClinicalUseDefinition as an active current resource. BR&R minutes show FHIR-31850 was reopened to define duration more precisely and later treated as pre-applied pending approval. Jira exact-path search found only FHIR-31850, and Zulip searches found no conflicting discussion. The original ClinicalUseIssue artifact name is explained by the adjacent FHIR-31847 rename to ClinicalUseDefinition.
reconciliation: No source files were changed. The active StructureDefinition already contains ClinicalUseDefinition.indication.duration[x] with the clarified definition and Range/string types, and no stale Quantity-only duration definition remains in the ClinicalUseDefinition source.
